context: You will hear a volunteer ranger giving information to visitors at a city park.

script.t: Hello and welcome to Greenfield Park. I'm Tom, one of the volunteer rangers here, and I'd like to tell you a little about the park and what you can do today.
The park was originally the garden of a large house, which was destroyed by fire in 1921. The land was bought by the city council in 1935, and it's been open to the public ever since.

Let me show you where things are on the map. As you come in through the main entrance, the visitor centre is immediately on your right. That's where you can pick up a free guide and find out about today's events.
If you turn left at the entrance and follow the path, you'll come to the playground, which was completely refurbished last summer.
Carry on along that path, past the playground, and you'll reach the rose garden, on the west side of the lake. It's at its best in June, so you've chosen a good time to visit.
Now, a lot of people expect the café to be near the entrance, but in fact it's on the far side of the lake, directly opposite the entrance. It has a lovely terrace overlooking the water.
And the toilets are in the north-east corner of the park, just behind the tennis courts.
A few things you should know. Cycling is allowed on the main paths, but not on the grass or around the lake. Dogs are welcome, but they must be kept on a lead near the playground.
Fishing in the lake used to be free, but since this spring you need a permit, which you can buy at the visitor centre for five pounds a day.
This afternoon there's a guided bird walk starting at two o'clock. It lasts about an hour and a half, and you don't need to book, just meet at the café.
We're also always looking for volunteers. Most of our volunteers help with planting and weeding, and we provide all the tools and training.
